title: Stateful Failsafe Orchestrator for Downstream Overload
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Add a stateful failsafe orchestration layer inside the runtime request path to protect customer SLOs during downstream overload (Redis/Kafka/primary DB). The component implements lease-based admission, optimistic local replicas for reads, ‘partial-response’ stubbing for large generation workloads, and coordinated circuit fences across regions. Goals: (1) keep tail latency and error-rate SLOs for high-priority tenants, (2) provide deterministic degradation profiles per tenant and route, (3) enable safe multi-region failover with minimal consistency surprises.
acceptance_criteria: Leases: runtime can issue per-tenant request leases and refuse requests when out of budget (configurable per release) without returning 500s
Partial-responses: for text generation routes, the orchestrator can return a documented ‘partial_response’ envelope that downstream clients can opt into
Read-stubs: read-path can serve recent cached or optimistic replica values for 95% of degraded-read scenarios with clear audit metrics
Circuit propagation: when a dependency circuit trips in region A, region B receives a propagated fence within 10s and applies the same degraded policy for affected tenants
No customer SLO regressions for P0 tenants in staging during 5 injected failure scenarios (Redis saturation, Kafka broker outage, DB read-only lock contention)
implementation_plan: Phase 1: Prototype lease token allocator in the local runtime (token bucket per-tenant + priority lanes)
Phase 2: Add read-stub layer: optimistic local replica with TTL-scoped entries + heuristics to favor strong reads for high-priority tenants
Phase 3: Add partial-response envelope for generator routes and API flagging in SDKs
Phase 4: Cross-region circuit fence: gossip channel + central control-plane bookmark for coordinated fallback
Phase 5: Integrate with existing autoscaler and Dedicated admission policies; add runbooks and dashboards
test_plan: Chaos scenarios (kafka failure, redis saturation, db slow queries) via chaosmonkey in staging
Synthetic load tests to verify admission fairness across tenants and priority lanes
Client compatibility tests for partial_response envelope (SDKs + sample apps)
Canary rollout in eu-west-1 with 5% traffic, monitor error and latency SLOs for 48h
Regression suite ensuring we do not increase token cost per 1k tokens by more than 2% for normal traffic
rollback_plan: Immediate feature toggle to disable orchestrator at edge and revert to legacy admission path
Automatic rollback trigger if p95 latency for any P0 route increases > 20% for 15m or error rate exceeds threshold
If cross-region fence causes correctness regressions, revert fence propagation and disable coordinated fallback until patch
progress_updates: 2026-03-01: Kickoff - scoped design and success criteria decided with PM and SRE; owner assigned (Marco Lin).
2026-03-04: Prototype of lease allocator implemented; basic token-bucket works for single-host; initial unit tests added.
2026-03-06: Design review with SRE and Product (notes in Confluence); agreed to make partial_response opt-in on API and SDK flag by default disabled.
2026-03-09: Implemented read-stub cache with LRU+TTL; observed 60% reduction in Redis read traffic under small load test (staging).
2026-03-12: Integration test uncovered edge-case where optimistic read returned stale value for multi-write tenant; added freshness window heuristic (50ms) as mitigation.
2026-03-14: Canary orchestration wiring completed, preparing canary rollout doc and alert thresholds.
decisions: Partial-response will use a documented envelope rather than changing core response types to make SDK integration explicit.
Lease admission is enforced at the runtime proxy layer, not at the model-serving process, to avoid model-level stalls.
Cross-region fence propagation uses the existing control-plane pub/sub with an eventual consistency window (target 10s) rather than strong consensus to keep latency low.
tradeoffs: Using optimistic replica reads increases the risk of stale reads; mitigated via per-tenant freshness windows and higher strictness for high-consistency tenants.
Partial responses improve availability but require client changes; made opt-in to reduce customer surprise.
Centralized fence coordination reduces divergence but introduces a new control-plane dependency; we accept an eventual consistency model to avoid adding a high-latency consensus step.
